newsitem.title: GERMANY: German economy seen hurt by failure of tax reform.
newsitem.headline: German economy seen hurt by failure of tax reform.

text.p: The German economy was headed for a difficult time attracting investment and fighting unemployment after Bonn's tax reform proposal died in a parliamentary deadlock, business leaders said on Thursday.
"The chance was wasted to make Germany more attractive in international competition for investment," said Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt in a statement.
The coalition had passed the 30 billion mark ($16 billion) tax-cutting package through the lower house of parliament, but opposition Social Democrats blocked it in the upper house.
In mediation on Wednesday, they agreed to eliminate a corporate trading tax, but ended talks early this morning deadlocked over the bulk of the plan.
"This is a disadvantage for Germany as a place of doing business," Rolf Peffekoven, a member of Bonn's council of economic advisers, told West German Radio.
The tax reform "would have led to an increase in investment, and that would have helped to fight unemployment, the main problem in the economy," he said.
Hans Peter Stihl, head of the German Federation of Chambers of Commerce (DIHT), said the SPD opposition was "a slap in the face to the economy."
Cutting the trading tax, which had collected nine billion marks from businesses, "was only a drop in the bucket," Stihl said.
